profiles.meeting_scenario: A preoperative planning meeting for a scheduled primary open rhinoplasty on a 27-year-old cosmetic patient with a moderate dorsal hump, bulbous underrotated tip, and mild alar flare. The attending facial plastic surgeon and the ambulatory OR coordinator are meeting three days before surgery to finalize the operative setup, room flow, materials to have available, and postoperative logistics for a same-day outpatient case. The agenda is to confirm the operative plan at a practical level, decide what the OR team should prepare, make sure visual planning materials will be available in the room, and align on recovery/discharge expectations. The expected outcome is a clear plan for case setup, staff preparation, patient flow, and who will handle each pre-op and post-op task.

members.name: Dr. Nina Patel
members.role: Attending facial plastic and reconstructive surgeon
members.expertise: Aesthetic nasal surgery, open rhinoplasty, tip shaping, component dorsal reduction
members.background: Board-certified plastic surgeon with a high-volume cosmetic nasal practice who routinely performs primary open rhinoplasty in an ambulatory surgery center and often relies on a familiar core rhinoplasty workflow.
members.private_state: She wants the case to run efficiently, preserve intraoperative flexibility for subtle alar base refinement if balance requires it, and avoid unnecessary back-and-forth with the OR team on the morning of surgery.
hidden_assumptions: At this center, a 'standard primary open rhinoplasty set' implicitly includes the extra fine instruments and minor add-ons she usually ends up needing for routine primary cases, including items that cover possible alar base refinement.
When people mention 'the clinic images,' they mean the full preoperative planning set she uses in surgery, including the Vectra morph printouts and selected goal views, not just the chart photos.
Saying 'get local in before we start' naturally means after induction but before prep and drape, so vasoconstriction develops while the face is being prepared.
For an uncomplicated outpatient rhinoplasty, 'routine discharge' means the patient goes home the same day once pain, nausea, and ordinary nasal oozing are controlled.

members.name: Lauren Brooks
members.role: Ambulatory OR coordinator and plastics service line RN
members.expertise: OR scheduling, surgical supply standardization, outpatient plastics workflow, PACU/discharge coordination
members.background: An experienced perioperative nurse who manages case preparation across multiple surgeons and relies on the center's standardized trays, charting systems, and ambulatory recovery protocols to keep rooms on time.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, on-time outpatient flow with no supply surprises, no unnecessary custom requests, and a recovery plan that fits the surgery center's standard discharge process.
hidden_assumptions: The center's 'standard rhinoplasty tray' means only the catalogued default tray and common nasal instruments; anything outside that set is a specific add-on that must be explicitly requested.
When surgeons ask for 'clinic images,' they usually mean the pre-op photographs already stored in the electronic chart and printable from the clinic visit.

If a surgeon says to get local in 'before we start,' that usually means after prep, drape, and timeout, immediately before incision, because room turnover begins as soon as anesthesia induces the patient.
A 'routine' outpatient discharge follows the nursing checklist for ambulatory facial cases, including a period of stable dressing output and other center-specific criteria before pickup is called.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the standard rhinoplasty setup
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the 'standard primary open rhinoplasty set.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the usual open rhinoplasty tray plus the small extras she informally treats as routine for primary cases, such as fine tip instruments, cartilage-shaping accessories, and items that would cover a modest alar base adjustment if she decides on it.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the facility's formally defined standard rhinoplasty tray only, with open nasal instruments, osteotomes, rasps, and default sutures; any alar base or special graft-prep items would need separate request lines.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds institutional and settled, so both assume there is one obvious shared meaning; prior cases may also have masked the gap when scrub staff informally added missing items without discussion.

misalignment_points.topic: Which preoperative images will be in the OR
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to having 'the clinic images' available in the room.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the consult planning packet she uses intraoperatively: the 3D morphing printouts and selected frontal/lateral goal images that guided the patient discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the standard pre-op photos already attached to the electronic chart from clinic, which can be printed easily for the room.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are literally talking about images from clinic, and either set would seem reasonable in casual conversation, so the difference feels too minor and routine to trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'get local in before we start.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means infiltration after induction and before prep/drape so the epinephrine has several minutes to work while the room is setting up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means infiltration after prep, drape, and timeout, immediately before incision, because that is still plainly 'before' the operative start in OR workflow terms.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each interpretation is common, both fit the phrase naturally, and the timing difference seems too operationally small to be worth spelling out during a competent planning discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the patient should have 'routine PACU recovery' and 'same-day discharge.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means discharge once the patient is comfortable, not nauseated, and showing only expected manageable mustache-dressing oozing for a rhinoplasty.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means discharge only after the ambulatory center's standard nursing thresholds are met, including a stable observation interval and other checklist items that may extend pickup timing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both think they are referencing the obvious normal course for an uncomplicated outpatient rhinoplasty, so neither experiences the phrase as requiring a formal definition.

turns.inner_thought: This is a routine primary cosmetic open rhinoplasty: component dorsal reduction, tip work for deprojection and rotation, likely some refinement of the domes, and I want the usual full setup I always have for these cases. In my mind the standard primary open rhinoplasty set already covers the finer tip instruments and the small extras I sometimes end up using, including what I'd want available if I decide on a subtle alar base refinement. I do not want a morning-of scramble over things that are basically routine in my practice.
turns.utterance: So for Friday, this is a straightforward primary open rhinoplasty. She has a moderate hump, a heavier underrotated tip, and a little base width, but overall it should be very standard. I’m planning an open approach, and we should be fine with the standard primary open rhinoplasty set.

turns.inner_thought: Good, if it's standard then I can keep this within the center's usual tray build and staffing pattern. I'll reserve the catalogued standard rhinoplasty tray and avoid custom supply requests unless she specifically asks. Also need to know what she wants for images; usually when surgeons say clinic images, they mean the chart photos from the office visit that we can print for the room.
turns.utterance: That works. You’re in the regular outpatient block, first case start, with our usual plastics team and a scrub who’s done plenty of rhinoplasties. I’ll reserve the standard rhinoplasty tray. Do you want the clinic images in the room as well?

turns.inner_thought: Yes, I definitely want the planning packet from clinic in the room—the Vectra morph printouts and the goal views are what help me check the dorsal aesthetic lines and where I want the tip to sit. And I want local placed after induction, before prep and drape, so the epinephrine has time to work while they are prepping. That's just the efficient way to run it.
turns.utterance: Yes, definitely have the clinic images available. They’ll help for the dorsal line and the tip rotation plan. And I like to get local in before we start.

turns.inner_thought: Easy enough—I can have the chart photos printed. On the local timing, that fits my normal OR flow: anesthesia induces, we get the patient prepped and draped, timeout, local goes in, then incision. That still counts as before we start, and it keeps turnover efficient instead of pausing the room right after induction.
turns.utterance: Perfect, I can have the clinic images printed. And once anesthesia induces, we can move straight into prep so the room keeps moving, then get local in before we start.

turns.inner_thought: I may or may not need a very small alar base refinement depending on how the tip and base balance after deprojection and rotation. To me that still falls under a routine primary case and should be covered by the standard primary open rhinoplasty set as I use it. No need to complicate this by turning it into a custom build discussion.
turns.utterance: Exactly. And I don’t expect anything unusual. If, once the tip is set, the tip-base relationship still feels a little wide, I may do a small routine finishing adjustment, but otherwise the setup should stay standard.

turns.inner_thought: Sounds like a normal outpatient plastics recovery as long as the case stays uncomplicated. I'll plan standard PACU workflow and the usual same-day process under our nursing criteria. Front desk should know it’s routine so pickup timing can be handled in the normal window, not rushed.
turns.utterance: Great. On the back end, I’ll plan for routine PACU recovery with same-day discharge and let the front desk know to expect the usual outpatient flow.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, she should absolutely go home the same day if she's comfortable, not nauseated, and just has the usual mild mustache-dressing oozing. I don't anticipate anything that should keep her longer. If PACU is uneventful, I'll do my standard evening check-in and that should be it.
turns.utterance: Yes, that’s what I’d expect. If recovery is routine, she should go home the same day. I usually do an evening check-in call if the PACU course is uneventful.

turns.inner_thought: I'll set expectations conservatively around our usual discharge sequence, meaning the escort should be available but understand there’s still the standard observation period and checklist before pickup is called. I’ll also make sure the standard facial plastics discharge instructions are ready and nothing special is missing.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I’ll tell the escort to expect the usual outpatient discharge timing, and I’ll make sure the standard postoperative instruction packet is ready.

turns.inner_thought: As long as the room has my usual full rhinoplasty setup, the proper planning images from clinic, and local is in early enough to blanch while prep is happening, the operation should move smoothly and stay on time. This all sounds aligned, so I don't need to drill into details.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Then with the standard primary open rhinoplasty set, the clinic images in the room, and local in before we start, I think this should stay very on schedule.

turns.inner_thought: Good, I have what I need: standard tray, printed clinic photos from the chart, routine outpatient recovery plan, no special requests flagged. I can finalize the room and staffing without building in custom supply lines or unusual discharge arrangements.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. I’ll finalize the room, supplies, printed materials, and the recovery plan based on what we discussed.
